transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good morning, Ms. Nguyen. It's been about three months since we started topiramate. How have the headaches been?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Better overall. I was having around twelve headache days a month, and now it's maybe five or six.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: That's a good drop. Are they still the same kind of headache, one-sided and throbbing?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, mostly on the left side, throbbing, and light bothers me. No aura, same as before.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: And when you get one, what do you take?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: The sumatriptan 50 mg. It works within an hour most of the time. I used it five times this month.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any side effects from the topiramate? Some people notice tingling in their fingers or trouble finding words.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: A little tingling in my fingers the first two weeks, but that's gone. No trouble with words.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Good. How are sleep and caffeine?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm sleeping about seven hours. I cut down to one coffee in the morning.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any new weakness, vision changes, or a sudden worst headache of your life?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Let me examine you. Blood pressure today is 118 over 76. Pupils are equal and reactive, the fundi look normal with no papilledema. Cranial nerves are intact, strength is 5 out of 5 throughout, reflexes are symmetric, and gait is normal.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: So this is chronic migraine without aura, improving on topiramate. Let's keep topiramate at 50 mg twice a day, and sumatriptan 50 mg as needed, but no more than nine days a month so you don't get rebound headaches.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Keep your headache diary, and we'll see you back in three months. If you get a sudden severe headache, new weakness, or vision loss, go to the emergency department.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Follow-up of chronic migraine, three months after starting topiramate.

sections.title: Interval history
sections.text: Headache days down from about twelve a month to five or six a month on topiramate. Headaches are left-sided and throbbing, and light bothers her; no aura. Sumatriptan 50 mg works within an hour; used five times this month. Tingling in the fingers in the first two weeks of topiramate, now gone; no trouble finding words. Sleeping about seven hours; cut down to one coffee in the morning. No new weakness, no vision changes, no sudden worst headache.

sections.title: Physical exam
sections.text: Blood pressure 118/76. Pupils equal and reactive. Fundi normal, no papilledema. Cranial nerves intact. Strength 5/5 throughout. Reflexes symmetric. Gait normal.

sections.title: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Chronic migraine without aura, improving on topiramate. Continue topiramate 50 mg twice a day. Continue sumatriptan 50 mg as needed, no more than nine days a month to avoid rebound headaches. Keep the headache diary. Follow-up in three months.

sections.title: Patient instructions
sections.text: Keep taking topiramate 50 mg twice a day. Take sumatriptan only as needed, no more than nine days a month. Keep your headache diary. Go to the emergency department for a sudden severe headache, new weakness, or vision loss. Return in three months.
